```{r phase9_paper_part3}
#            for it; 9.19F passes the registered scores' labels).
pa_h11_summary <- function(sub, grouping_label, punit = PA_PUNIT,
                           lab = if (punit == PA_PUNIT) PA_LAB else PA_LAB_SR) {
  h1 <- run_h1(sub, punit = punit); h2 <- run_h2(sub, punit = punit)
  h3 <- run_h3(sub); h4 <- run_h4(sub); h5 <- run_h5(sub)
  h7 <- pa_relabel_h7(run_h7(sub)); h8 <- run_h8(sub, punit = punit)
  h9 <- paired_test(sub, "retribution_items", "revenge", alternative = "greater", label = "")
  h10 <- pa_h10_run(sub, punit, punit)
  p6 <- cor_row(sub, "retribution_items", "proportionality_principle", alternative = "two.sided")
  s6 <- cor_row(sub, "retribution_items", "severity_index", alternative = "two.sided")
  st6 <- steiger_overlap(sub, "retribution_items", "severity_index",
                         "proportionality_principle", alternative = "two.sided", label = "")
  rev <- h7[h7$y == "Revenge", ]; ret <- h7[h7$y == PA_DT, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(rev) == 6, nrow(ret) == 6)
  v <- c(
    H1_n_positive_of_12 = sum(h1$r > 0), H1_n_BH_significant = sum(h1$p_BH_one_sided < .05),
    H1_min_r = min(h1$r), H1_max_r = max(h1$r),
    H2_diff = h2$diff, H2_diff_lower = h2$diff_lower, H2_diff_upper = h2$diff_upper,
    H2_z = h2$z, H2_p_one_sided = h2$p,
    H3_n_positive_of_66 = sum(h3$cor_matrix[upper.tri(h3$cor_matrix)] > 0),
    H3_share_1 = h3$var_explained_1,
    H4_item_d = h4$tests$d[1], H4_item_p_one_sided = h4$tests$p_dir[1],
    H5_d = h5$d[1], H5_p_one_sided = h5$p_dir[1],
    H6_r_principle = p6$r, H6_r_severity = s6$r, H6_diff = st6$diff,
    H6_diff_lower = st6$diff_lower, H6_diff_upper = st6$diff_upper, H6_p_two = st6$p,
    H7_revenge_n_p05_of_6 = sum(rev$p_directional < .05), H7_revenge_min_r = min(rev$r),
    H7_revenge_max_r = max(rev$r),
    H7_desert_theory_n_positive_of_6 = sum(ret$r > 0),
    H7_desert_theory_n_two_sided_p05 = sum(ret$p_two < .05),
    H7_desert_theory_min_r = min(ret$r), H7_desert_theory_max_r = max(ret$r),
    H8_n_p05_of_6 = sum(h8$p_one_sided < .05), H8_min_r = min(h8$r), H8_max_r = max(h8$r),
    H9_d = h9$d, H9_d_lower = h9$d_lower, H9_d_upper = h9$d_upper, H9_p_one_sided = h9$p_dir,
    H10_diff = h10$diff[2], H10_diff_lower = h10$diff_lower[2],
    H10_diff_upper = h10$diff_upper[2], H10_z = h10$z[2], H10_p_two = h10$p[2],
    H10_p_one_sided_registered_direction = h10$p[1])
  data.frame(grouping = grouping_label, punitiveness = lab, n = nrow(sub),
             quantity = names(v), value = unname(v), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
pa_h11_subs <- list(
  "Whole sample (reference)" = pa_d,
  "Ranking (retribution first)" = pa_retrib,
  "Median split: high half" = pa_d[!is.na(pa_d$grp_med) & pa_d$grp_med == "High rel. retribution", ],
  "Tertiles: top third" = pa_d[!is.na(pa_d$grp_tert) & pa_d$grp_tert == "Top third", ],
  "Sentencing ratio: did not reduce" =
    pa_d[!is.na(pa_d$grp_ratio) & pa_d$grp_ratio == "High sentencing ratio", ])
# GUARD: the subsets are the same people, in the same order, that 9.17E uses.
stopifnot(identical(unname(lapply(pa_h11_subs[-1], `[[`, "ResponseId")),
                    unname(lapply(p3_sub, `[[`, "ResponseId"))))
pa_ratio_g <- "Sentencing ratio: did not reduce"
pa_h11_groupings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_h11_subs), function(g)
  suppressWarnings(pa_h11_summary(pa_h11_subs[[g]], g,
                                  punit = if (g == pa_ratio_g) PA_PUNIT_SR else PA_PUNIT))))
# GUARD: no row of the ratio grouping uses the six-part score, and every other
# row does.
stopifnot(all(pa_h11_groupings$punitiveness[pa_h11_groupings$grouping == pa_ratio_g] == PA_LAB_SR),
          all(pa_h11_groupings$punitiveness[pa_h11_groupings$grouping != pa_ratio_g] == PA_LAB))
# GUARD: the ranking rows agree with the separate H11 runs above.
pa_g <- function(q) pa_h11_groupings$value[pa_h11_groupings$grouping == "Ranking (retribution first)" &
                                            pa_h11_groupings$quantity == q]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_g("H2_diff"), pa_h11_h2$diff)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_g("H10_diff"), pa_h11_h10$diff[2])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_g("H9_d"), pa_h11_h9$d)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_g("H3_share_1"), pa_h11_h3_sum$share_1)))
TABLES[["PAPER_H11_groupings"]] <- pa_h11_groupings

# --- H12: each hostile attitude's correlation with punitiveness -------------------
# 9.2's correlations inside the retributivist group, and 9.17C's on the
# retributive side of the other three groupings, with the six-part score as
# punitiveness. H12 names no direction, so the two-sided p is the one reported.
# The shares endorsing each attitude do not involve punitiveness and do not
# change.
pa_h12_sides <- list(
  "Ranking (retribution first)" = pa_d$grp_rank == "Retributivist",
  "Median split, upper half"    = pa_d$grp_med  == "High rel. retribution",
  "Top third"                   = pa_d$grp_tert == "Top third",
  "Sentencing ratio, kept or raised" = pa_d$grp_ratio == "High sentencing ratio")
# As in H11 above, punitiveness under the ratio grouping is the standardized
# five-part score. `lab` names the punitiveness score in the export; by default
# the paper's label for the column passed (9.19F passes the registered
# scores' labels).
pa_h12_run <- function(sub, g, punit, lab = NULL) {
  if (is.null(lab)) lab <- ifelse(punit == PA_PUNIT, PA_LAB, PA_LAB_SR)
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(h12_spec)), function(i)
    cor_row(sub, punit, h12_spec$var[i], alternative = "greater",
            label_x = lab, label_y = h12_spec$label[i]))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- cor_row(sub, punit, "shark_kill", alternative = "greater",
                                      label_x = lab, label_y = "Putting the shark to death (yes)")
  cbind(grouping = g, do.call(rbind, rows))
}
pa_h12_ratio <- "Sentencing ratio, kept or raised"
pa_h12 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_h12_sides), function(g)
  pa_h12_run(pa_d[pa_h12_sides[[g]] %in% TRUE, ], g,
             if (g == pa_h12_ratio) PA_PUNIT_SR else PA_PUNIT)))
# GUARDS.
#   1. Each grouping's subset is the same people 9.17C uses.
#   2. The function, run on the registered retributivists (d_retrib) with the
#      registered eight-item scale, reproduces 9.2's ranking rows exactly, so
#      the exported rows differ from 9.2 only in the punitiveness score.
#   3. The ratio rows use the standardized five-part score and the others the
#      six-part score.
stopifnot(identical(unname(lapply(pa_h12_sides, function(s) pa_d$ResponseId[s %in% TRUE])),
                    unname(lapply(p3_sub, `[[`, "ResponseId"))))
pa_h12_chk <- pa_h12_run(d_retrib, "check", "punitiveness", lab = "check")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_h12_chk$r[seq_len(nrow(h12_spec))],
                           h12$r_with_punitiveness[match(h12_spec$label, h12$attitude)])),
          all(pa_h12$x[pa_h12$grouping == pa_h12_ratio] == PA_LAB_SR),
          all(pa_h12$x[pa_h12$grouping != pa_h12_ratio] == PA_LAB))
TABLES[["PAPER_H12_cors"]] <- pa_h12
show_table(pa_h12[pa_h12$grouping == "Ranking (retribution first)",
                  c("y", "n", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_two")],
           "9.19D: H12, each attitude with punitiveness (six-part score) among retributivists")

# --- The contrast sets ------------------------------------------------------------
# pa_spec (9.19A) labels the two H21 rows with the paper's scores; every other
# row, and the order of the rows, is the registered spec's.
pa_contrasts <- list(
  rank  = run_contrast_set(pa_d, "grp_rank", spec = pa_spec),
  med   = run_contrast_set(pa_d, "grp_med", spec = pa_spec),
  tert  = run_contrast_set(pa_d, "grp_tert", spec = pa_spec),
  ratio = run_contrast_set(pa_d, "grp_ratio", spec = pa_spec, drop_sentence_based = TRUE))
# The deterrence- and incapacitation-first comparison, the main text's: 9.12b's
# grouping column, carried onto pa_d. Its retributive side is the 371 who
# ranked retribution first; its other side is the 453 who ranked deterrence or
# incapacitation first, and the 124 who ranked rehabilitation first are left
# out (NA).
pa_cq_d <- pa_d
pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap <- cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap
stopifnot(identical(pa_cq_d$ResponseId, cq_d$ResponseId))
pa_contrasts$vs_deter_incap <- run_contrast_set(pa_cq_d, "grp_vs_deter_incap", spec = pa_spec)
pa_cont <- list(
  rel   = run_continuous_set(pa_d, "retribution_rel", spec = pa_spec),
  raw   = run_continuous_set(pa_d, "retribution", spec = pa_spec),
  ratio = pa_cont_ratio,
  resid = run_continuous_set(pa_d, "sentence_resid", spec = pa_spec,
                             drop_sentence_based = TRUE))

# GUARDS. The exports carry the PAPER_ name so the write-up reads one family of
# files; the paper's choices are in the counts below.
#   1. Every row that is not punitiveness reproduces its registered counterpart
#      row for row, since no other contrast outcome reads a rescored column;
#      and each run has the registered rows in the registered order.
#   2. The punitiveness rows are the same test on 7.4's part scores (p5_d,
#      carrying the grouping columns of d, and 9.12b's comparison column),
#      under the paper's labels; the six-part row is present exactly where the
#      registered run has the full-index row (it drops out of the runs built
#      from the sentence).
#   3. Under the ranking, the six-part d also reproduces 9.17's independent
#      rescoring (P3_rescored_contrasts).
pa_p_labs <- c(PA_LAB, PA_LAB_SR)
pa_chk_d  <- p5_d
stopifnot(identical(pa_chk_d$ResponseId, cq_d$ResponseId))
pa_chk_d$grp_vs_deter_incap <- cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap
pa_p_col <- c(punitiveness_full = "punit_parts6", punitiveness = "punit_parts5z")
pa_grp <- c(rank = "grp_rank", med = "grp_med", tert = "grp_tert", ratio = "grp_ratio",
            vs_deter_incap = "grp_vs_deter_incap")
pa_reg <- list(rank = contrasts_rank, med = contrasts_med, tert = contrasts_tert,
               ratio = contrasts_ratio, vs_deter_incap = cq_contrasts)
for (g in names(pa_reg)) {
  a <- pa_contrasts[[g]]; b <- pa_reg[[g]]
  keep <- !(a$outcome %in% pa_p_labs)
  stopifnot(identical(a$variable, b$variable), identical(a$outcome[keep], b$outcome[keep]),
            isTRUE(all.equal(a$d[keep], b$d[keep])),
            isTRUE(all.equal(a$p_dir[keep], b$p_dir[keep])),
            identical(PA_LAB %in% a$outcome, "punitiveness_full" %in% b$variable))
  for (i in which(!keep)) {
    chk <- welch_contrast(pa_chk_d, pa_p_col[[a$variable[i]]], pa_grp[[g]],
                          alternative = "greater", label = a$outcome[i])
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(c(a$d[i], a$t[i], a$p_dir[i]), c(chk$d, chk$t, chk$p_dir))))
  }
}
pa_p3_six <- TABLES[["P3_rescored_contrasts"]]
pa_p3_six <- pa_p3_six$estimate[pa_p3_six$run == "Ranking (primary)" &
                                pa_p3_six$outcome == "Punitiveness, six parts weighted equally (with the sentence)"]
stopifnot(length(pa_p3_six) == 1,
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_contrasts$rank$d[pa_contrasts$rank$outcome == PA_LAB], pa_p3_six)))
pa_reg_cont <- list(rel = cont_rel, raw = cont_raw, ratio = cont_ratio, resid = cont_resid)
pa_pred <- c(rel = "retribution_rel", raw = "retribution", ratio = "sentence_ratio",
             resid = "sentence_resid")
for (g in names(pa_reg_cont)) {
  a <- pa_cont[[g]]; b <- pa_reg_cont[[g]]
  keep <- !(a$outcome %in% pa_p_labs)
  stopifnot(identical(a$hypothesis, b$hypothesis), identical(a$outcome[keep], b$outcome[keep]),
            isTRUE(all.equal(a$beta[keep], b$beta[keep])),
            identical(PA_LAB %in% a$outcome,
                      contrast_spec$label[contrast_spec$outcome == "punitiveness_full"] %in% b$outcome))
  for (i in which(!keep)) {
    col <- if (a$outcome[i] == PA_LAB) "punit_parts6" else "punit_parts5z"
    chk <- cont_reg(p5_d, col, pa_pred[[g]], alternative = "greater")
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(a$beta[i], chk$beta)))
  }
}
# In the exports, the `variable` column of the two punitiveness rows names the
# score's own column in 7.4 (punit_parts6, punit_parts5z) rather than the pa_d
# column that carried it under a registered name, so that no reader of the file
# takes those rows for the registered scores. (The continuous runs have no
# `variable` column; their labels say which score each row carries.)
pa_var_out <- function(x) {
  i <- x$variable %in% names(pa_p_col)
  x$variable[i] <- unname(pa_p_col[x$variable[i]])
  x
}
for (g in names(pa_contrasts)) TABLES[[paste0("PAPER_contrasts_", g)]] <- pa_var_out(pa_contrasts[[g]])
for (g in names(pa_cont))      TABLES[[paste0("PAPER_cont_", g)]]      <- pa_cont[[g]]

# The shark decision (H15's yes-or-no item), the one registered outcome outside
# the contrast set: the share answering yes on each side of the main text's
# comparison, with exact intervals. The logistic test of the difference is
# 9.12b's cq_h15 (H15_logistic_vs_deter_incap).
pa_shark <- rbind(
  cbind(side = "Ranked retribution first",
        prop_ci(pa_cq_d$shark_kill[pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap %in% "Retributivist"],
                "Putting the shark to death (yes)")),
  cbind(side = "Ranked deterrence or incapacitation first",
        prop_ci(pa_cq_d$shark_kill[pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap %in% "Deterrence or incapacitation first"],
                "Putting the shark to death (yes)")))
# GUARD: the two sides are the 371 and the 453.
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(pa_shark$n), c(371L, 453L)))
TABLES[["PAPER_shark_vs_deter_incap"]] <- pa_shark
show_table(pa_contrasts$vs_deter_incap[, c("hypothesis", "outcome", "n1", "n2", "M1", "M2", "t",
                                           "df", "p_dir", "d", "d_lower", "d_upper")],
           "9.19D: retributivists against the deterrence- or incapacitation-first (one-sided)")
show_table(pa_shark, "9.19D: the shark decision on each side of that comparison")

# The share endorsing each attitude H12 lists (a mean above 4, the scale
# midpoint) and the share answering yes to the shark decision, among the
# participants who ranked deterrence or incapacitation first (n = 453), the
# main text's comparison group. 9.17C gives the same shares for everyone else
# under the ranking (P3_H12_everyone_else); the paper's figure of H12 sets the
# retributivists beside this narrower group instead. NOT REGISTERED and
# descriptive: H12 concerns retributivists only, and no difference in shares
# is tested. Exact (Clopper-Pearson) intervals from prop_ci(), as in 9.17C.
pa_di <- pa_cq_d[pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap %in% "Deterrence or incapacitation first", ]
stopifnot(nrow(pa_di) == 453)
pa_h12_di <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(h12_spec)), function(i)
  prop_ci(as.integer(pa_di[[h12_spec$var[i]]] > 4), h12_spec$label[i])))
pa_h12_di <- rbind(pa_h12_di, prop_ci(pa_di$shark_kill, "Putting the shark to death (yes)"))
names(pa_h12_di) <- c("attitude", "n", "k_endorsing", "share", "share_ci_lower", "share_ci_upper")
# GUARDS.
#   1. The same rule applied to everyone else under the ranking reproduces
#      9.17C's shares, so the only thing that differs here is the group.
#   2. The attitudes are 9.17C's, in 9.17C's order, so the figure can match
#      the two exports row for row.
pa_other_chk <- pa_d[pa_d$grp_rank %in% "Other", ]
pa_other_share <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(h12_spec)), function(i)
  mean(pa_other_chk[[h12_spec$var[i]]] > 4, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_other_share, p3_h12_other$share[seq_len(nrow(h12_spec))])),
          identical(pa_h12_di$attitude, p3_h12_other$attitude))
TABLES[["PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap"]] <- pa_h12_di
show_table(pa_h12_di, "9.19D: H12's attitudes among the deterrence- or incapacitation-first (descriptive; not registered)")

# --- The counts the Part 3 text uses (9.17B, on the paper's scorings) -------------
# p3_score() counts, over the registered rows, the E1 rows and every row, how many
# take the predicted sign, how many reach one-sided p < .05, how many intervals
# clear zero, and the median absolute effect. Nothing new is tested. 9.17B's
# three row sets are kept; three more follow the paper's scorings.
#   - Registered (H13 to H21), punitiveness once: H21 has two rows, here the
#     standardized five-part score and the six-part score. The paper counts
#     punitiveness once, as the six-part score wherever the run has that row,
#     and as the five-part score only where the six-part score is dropped
#     (the runs built from the sentence).
#   - E1, two-item reflection score: the E1 rows with the two-item score in
#     place of the three-item one.
#   - All rows, paper scorings: the two sets above together.
pa_crt3 <- contrast_spec$label[contrast_spec$outcome == "CRT"]
pa_sr   <- pa_spec$label[pa_spec$outcome == "punitiveness"]
pa_full <- pa_spec$label[pa_spec$outcome == "punitiveness_full"]
stopifnot(length(pa_crt3) == 1, length(pa_sr) == 1, length(pa_full) == 1)
pa_reg_once <- function(r) r$hypothesis %in% paste0("H", 13:21) &
  !(r$outcome == pa_sr & pa_full %in% r$outcome[!is.na(r$d %||% r$beta)])
pa_e1_two   <- function(r) r$hypothesis == "E1" & r$outcome != pa_crt3
pa_row_sets <- c(p3_row_sets, list(
  "Registered (H13 to H21), punitiveness once" = pa_reg_once,
  "E1, two-item reflection score" = pa_e1_two,
  "All rows, paper scorings" = function(r) pa_reg_once(r) | pa_e1_two(r)))
# The same counting rule as 9.17B's p3_score(), with the row sets passed in
# rather than read from 9.17B, so that 9.17B's own definition is never touched.
pa_score <- function(res, est, lo, hi, run_label, sets = pa_row_sets) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sets), function(s) {
    r <- res[sets[[s]](res) & !is.na(res[[est]]), ]
    pred   <- ifelse(r$alternative == "less", r[[est]] < 0, r[[est]] > 0)
    clears <- ifelse(r$alternative == "less", r[[hi]] < 0, r[[lo]] > 0)
    data.frame(run = run_label, row_set = s, n_rows = nrow(r),
               n_predicted_sign = sum(pred),
               n_one_sided_p05 = sum(r$p_dir < .05),
               n_interval_clears_zero = sum(clears),
               median_abs_estimate = median(abs(r[[est]])),
               statistic = est, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}
# GUARD: on the registered ranking run, this rule reproduces 9.17B's scorecard
# for the row sets 9.17B defines.
pa_chk_sc <- pa_score(contrasts_rank, "d", "d_lower", "d_upper", "Ranking (primary)",
                      sets = p3_row_sets)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_chk_sc,
                           p3_scorecard[p3_scorecard$run == "Ranking (primary)", ],
                           check.attributes = FALSE)))
pa_scorecard <- rbind(
  pa_score(pa_contrasts$rank,  "d", "d_lower", "d_upper", "Ranking (primary)"),
  pa_score(pa_contrasts$med,   "d", "d_lower", "d_upper", "Median split"),
  pa_score(pa_contrasts$tert,  "d", "d_lower", "d_upper", "Tertiles"),
  pa_score(pa_contrasts$ratio, "d", "d_lower", "d_upper", "Sentencing ratio grouping"),
  pa_score(pa_contrasts$vs_deter_incap, "d", "d_lower", "d_upper",
           "Ranking, against deterrence- or incapacitation-first (not registered)"),
  pa_score(pa_cont$rel,   "beta", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "Relative retribution, continuous"),
  pa_score(pa_cont$raw,   "beta", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "Retribution subscale, continuous"),
  pa_score(pa_cont$ratio, "beta", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "Sentencing ratio, continuous"),
  pa_score(pa_cont$resid, "beta", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",
           "Second sentence residualized on the first, continuous"))
# GUARD: punitiveness is counted once in the paper's registered set: 20 rows in
# each run that has both H21 rows, 19 in the runs built from the sentence.
pa_once <- pa_scorecard[pa_scorecard$row_set == "Registered (H13 to H21), punitiveness once", ]
stopifnot(all(pa_once$n_rows == ifelse(grepl("ratio|residualized", pa_once$run), 19, 20)))
TABLES[["PAPER_scorecard"]] <- pa_scorecard
show_table(pa_scorecard, "9.19D: each run counted over its rows, on the paper's scorings")

# Which rows (registered and E1) reach one-sided p < .05 under all four
# groupings, with one added row for punitiveness as the paper counts it: the
# six-part score under the ranking, the median split and the tertiles, and the
# standardized five-part score under the ratio grouping, which drops the
# six-part score.
pa_rows <- data.frame(hypothesis = pa_spec$hypothesis,
                      outcome = pa_spec$label, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
for (g in c("rank", "med", "tert", "ratio")) {
  r <- pa_contrasts[[g]][match(pa_rows$outcome, pa_contrasts[[g]]$outcome), ]
  pa_rows[[paste0("p05_", g)]] <- r$p_dir < .05
  pa_rows[[paste0("d_", g)]]   <- r$d
}
pa_pc <- grep("^p05_", names(pa_rows), value = TRUE)
pa_rows$n_groupings_run <- rowSums(!is.na(pa_rows[, pa_pc]))
pa_rows$holds_p05_every_grouping_run <- rowSums(pa_rows[, pa_pc], na.rm = TRUE) ==
  pa_rows$n_groupings_run
pa_merge <- pa_rows[pa_rows$outcome == pa_full, ]
pa_merge$outcome <- "Punitiveness as the paper counts it (six components; five attitude components under the ratio)"
stopifnot(is.na(pa_merge$p05_ratio))
pa_merge[, c("p05_ratio", "d_ratio")] <- pa_rows[pa_rows$outcome == pa_sr, c("p05_ratio", "d_ratio")]
pa_merge$n_groupings_run <- sum(!is.na(unlist(pa_merge[, pa_pc])))
pa_merge$holds_p05_every_grouping_run <- all(unlist(pa_merge[, pa_pc]))
pa_rows <- rbind(pa_rows, pa_merge)
TABLES[["PAPER_rows_across_groupings"]] <- pa_rows
```

```{r phase9_paper_dan_queries}
# === 9.19E RETRIBUTIVISTS AND THE OTHERS ON PROPORTIONALITY AND REVENGE ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: answers three questions Dan Simon put on 26 Sep 2026.
#   1. Do desert theory and proportionality go together among retributivists
#      (and among the other participants)?
#   2. Do retributivists differ from the other participants on support for
#      proportionality and for departing from it?
#   3. Do retributivists differ from the other participants on revenge?
# Questions 2 and 3 are asked against two comparison groups: all other
# participants, and the other participants without those who ranked
# rehabilitation first (that is, the deterrence- and incapacitation-first
# participants of 9.12b). Produces PAPER_dan_hang_together and
# PAPER_dan_contrasts.
# It also answers two further questions for Supplement Section S5 and its
# Table S19 (these back the paper's General Discussion):
#   4. Do retributivists reject parsimony (the limit that punishment be no
#      heavier than necessary) more than the others do? Two rows appended to
#      PAPER_dan_contrasts, one per comparison group (section 2b below).
#   5. Do retributivists agree with the proportionality principle as often as
#      the others do, counting agreement as a rating above 4? Shares and their
#      differences, in the new export PAPER_dan_prop_shares (section 4 below).
# PAPER CLAIMS BACKED HERE. General Discussion: "five in six retributivists
#   agreed with it. But note that similar levels of agreement were reported
#   also by the other participants" (question 5), and "retributivists were less
#   disinclined to do so than the other participants" (question 2, severity_1,
#   a difference in means). Supplement S5, "The registered comparison under the
#   features of retributive theory", paragraphs Proportionality (questions 2
#   and 5) and Leniency (question 4), and the rows of Table S19 headed "Not
#   registered (two-sided)".
# DANGER: the first half of that General Discussion sentence, "while a majority
#   of all participants resisted the notion of punishing beyond the severity of
#   the crime", is NOT backed here: nothing in this chunk counts shares on
#   severity_1. It holds for the whole sample only, by H4's shares (8.1,
#   H4_shares: 421 of 948, 44.4%, answered at or above the midpoint, so 55.6%
#   answered below it). Among the retributivists alone, fewer than half answered
#   below the midpoint (9.1, H11_H4_shares: 197 of 371, 53.1%, at or above it).
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED. Every test here is two-sided, because none of these
#         comparisons was registered with a direction. The registered H11 test
#         of question 1 (desert against the proportionality component inside
#         the retributivist group) is h11_h6 in 9.1, repeated here beside the
#         paper's scoring for comparison.
# CONSUMES: pa_d, pa_retrib, pa_cq_d, pa_contrasts, PA_DT, PA_DESERT_REG,
#           pa_spec (9.19A, 9.19D); d (registered scorings); cor_row(),
#           steiger_overlap(), welch_contrast(), prop_ci() (0.3); h11_h6 (9.1);
#           pa_h11_h6, pa_h11_h6_st (9.19D); p5_d, p5_parts (7.4);
#           h4_full (8.1) and h11_h4 (9.1) for the share guards.
# WRITES: TABLES[["PAPER_dan_hang_together"]], TABLES[["PAPER_dan_contrasts"]]
#         (its first 14 rows as before, then the two parsimony rows) and
#         TABLES[["PAPER_dan_prop_shares"]] (new).

# --- 1. Do they go together, and in whom? ---------------------------------------
# Correlations of desert theory with the proportionality principle (the direct
# item) and with the severity index (the two departure items, high =
# punishment at or above the offense), and the Steiger comparison between them,
# in each group. The registered pair, desert (items 1 to 4) with the three-item
# proportionality component, is added from d.
pa_groups_q1 <- list(
  "Retributivists (ranked retribution first)" = pa_d$grp_rank == "Retributivist",
  "All other participants"                    = pa_d$grp_rank == "Other",
  "Deterrence- or incapacitation-first"       =
    pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap == "Deterrence or incapacitation first")
pa_q1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_groups_q1), function(g) {
  keep <- pa_groups_q1[[g]] %in% TRUE
  sub <- pa_d[keep, ]; sub_reg <- d[keep, ]
  st <- steiger_overlap(sub, "retribution_items", "severity_index",
                        "proportionality_principle", alternative = "two.sided", label = "")
  rbind(
    cbind(group = g, pair = paste(PA_DT, "with the proportionality principle"),
          cor_row(sub, "retribution_items", "proportionality_principle", alternative = "two.sided")),
    cbind(group = g, pair = paste(PA_DT, "with the severity index"),
          cor_row(sub, "retribution_items", "severity_index", alternative = "two.sided")),
    cbind(group = g, pair = paste(PA_DESERT_REG, "with the registered proportionality component"),
          cor_row(sub_reg, "deserved", "proportionality_jd", alternative = "two.sided")),
    data.frame(group = g, pair = "Severity index minus principle (Steiger)", x = NA, y = NA,
               n = st$n, r = st$diff, ci_lower = st$diff_lower, ci_upper = st$diff_upper,
               p_two = st$p, p_dir = st$p, alternative = "two.sided", stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}))
# GUARD: the registered retributivist row reproduces 9.1's H11 test of H6, and
# the paper's retributivist rows reproduce 9.19D.
pa_q1_ret <- pa_q1[pa_q1$group == "Retributivists (ranked retribution first)", ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_q1_ret$r[3], h11_h6$cor$r)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_q1_ret$r[1:2], pa_h11_h6$r)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_q1_ret$r[4], pa_h11_h6_st$diff)))
TABLES[["PAPER_dan_hang_together"]] <- pa_q1
show_table(pa_q1[, c("group", "pair", "n", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_two")],
           "9.19E: do desert theory and proportionality go together? (two-sided)")

# --- 2 and 3. Retributivists against the others -----------------------------------
# Welch t tests with Cohen's d, two-sided. Retributivists are the first group,
# so a positive d means retributivists score higher. Measures:
#   proportionality principle: "Punishment should be proportionate to the
#     severity of the crime, no more and no less" (1 to 7);
#   severity_1: "Punishment should be greater than the seriousness of the crime";
#   severity_2: "Punishment should be less severe than the harmfulness of the
#     crime" (as answered, not reversed);
#   severity index: severity_1 and severity_2 reversed, averaged (high = at or
#     above the offense, never below);
#   the registered proportionality component (the direct item with both
#     departures reversed);
#   revenge on its four registered items, the paper's score, and on Study 1's
#     three items.
pa_q23_vars <- c(proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle",
                 severity_1 = "Punish more than the crime (severity_1)",
                 severity_2 = "Punish less than the harm (severity_2, as answered)",
                 severity_index = "Severity index",
                 proportionality_jd = "Registered proportionality component",
                 revenge = "Revenge, four items (paper, as registered)",
                 revenge3 = "Revenge, three items (rescoring)")
stopifnot(all(names(pa_q23_vars) %in% names(pa_d)), all(names(pa_q23_vars) %in% names(pa_cq_d)))
pa_q23 <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_q23_vars), function(v) cbind(
    comparison = "Retributivists vs all other participants",
    welch_contrast(pa_d, v, "grp_rank", alternative = "two.sided", label = pa_q23_vars[[v]])))),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_q23_vars), function(v) cbind(
    comparison = "Retributivists vs deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)",
    welch_contrast(pa_cq_d, v, "grp_vs_deter_incap", alternative = "two.sided",
                   label = pa_q23_vars[[v]])))))
# GUARD: the revenge rows reproduce the contrast sets of 9.19D, which ran the
# same Welch test one-sided (so t, df and d agree; only p differs).
pa_rv <- function(set) set[set$outcome == unname(pa_spec$label[pa_spec$outcome == "revenge"]), ]
pa_q23_rv <- pa_q23[pa_q23$variable == "revenge", ]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_q23_rv$d, c(pa_rv(pa_contrasts$rank)$d,
                                          pa_rv(pa_contrasts$vs_deter_incap)$d))),
          !anyNA(pa_q23$d))

# --- 2b. Rejection of parsimony: retributivists against the others ---------------
# WHAT THIS COMPUTES: the same Welch t test and Cohen's d (unpooled SD, with
#   its 95% interval) as the rows above, two-sided, on REJECTION OF PARSIMONY,
#   one of the six components of punitiveness. Parsimony is the limit that
#   punishment be no heavier than necessary. It was measured by two items,
#   parsimony_1 ("Criminal punishments should be as light as possible") and
#   parsimony_2 ("The state should not punish more than is absolutely
#   necessary"). The component is the mean of the two items REVERSED
#   (parsimony_1_R, parsimony_2_R; 8 minus the answer on the 1 to 7 scale), so
#   a high score means rejecting the limit, the more punitive answer.
# READS: p5_parts$parsimony_rejected, built in 7.4 exactly as the punitiveness
#   scores use it (p5_d$punit_parts6 and punit_parts5z average it with the other
#   components); pa_d$grp_rank (all 577 others) and pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap
#   (the 453 who ranked deterrence or incapacitation first).
# WRITES: two rows appended to pa_q23, and so to PAPER_dan_contrasts, in the
#   order of the rows above (all other participants first).
# PAPER CLAIM: Supplement S5, Leniency, and the row of Table S19 headed "Not
#   registered (two-sided): Leniency".
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED, two-sided. And NOT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE: rejection of
#   parsimony is one of the six components averaged into the punitiveness
#   score, whose contrast is H21 (and one of the five attitude components of
#   punitiveness without the sentence). This contrast is therefore part of what
#   the punitiveness contrast already shows, and the Supplement says so.
# DANGER: build it from p5_parts$parsimony_rejected (the reversed items). The
#   raw parsimony_1 and parsimony_2 columns, which 8.3c uses on purpose because
#   there the question is whether people ACCEPT the limit, would turn the sign
#   of this contrast upside down. The guards below check the reversal and the
#   component, item by item.
# DANGER: the new rows are APPENDED after the 14 rows above, never inserted
#   into pa_q23_vars. Inserting them there would interleave them with the
#   existing rows and change the export's existing lines, which the
#   Supplement's other numbers are read from.
# DANGER: the parsimony column goes on private copies (pa_par_d, pa_par_cq_d),
#   never on pa_d or pa_cq_d. pa_d is the paper's scored copy of d, which 9.19A
#   guards to differ from d in named columns only and which the later 9.19
#   chunks read and copy (9.19F's pa_old_d among them); a stray column there
#   would travel into every one of those copies.
# GUARDS.
#   1. Rows line up: p5_d (whose rows p5_parts shares) is the same participants
#      in the same order as pa_d and pa_cq_d.
#   2. The reversal: each _R item is 8 minus the raw answer, and the component
#      is the plain mean of the two reversed items for every participant (no
#      one is missing an item, so the at-least-half rule never applies).
#   3. The component is the one the six-part punitiveness score averages:
#      punit_parts6 equals the mean of the standardized p5_parts columns (this
#      one among them) and the standardized sentence.
stopifnot(nrow(p5_parts) == nrow(pa_d),
          identical(p5_d$ResponseId, pa_d$ResponseId),
          identical(pa_cq_d$ResponseId, pa_d$ResponseId))
stopifnot(!anyNA(d$parsimony_1), !anyNA(d$parsimony_2),
          isTRUE(all.equal(d$parsimony_1_R, 8 - d$parsimony_1)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(d$parsimony_2_R, 8 - d$parsimony_2)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(p5_parts$parsimony_rejected,
                           rowMeans(d[, c("parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R")]))))
pa_par_z <- as.data.frame(scale(p5_parts))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  p5_d$punit_parts6,
  rowMeans(data.frame(pa_par_z, s = as.numeric(scale(d$Sentence1_z)))))))
pa_par_lab <- "Rejection of parsimony (a component of punitiveness)"
pa_par_d    <- pa_d;    pa_par_d$parsimony_rejected    <- p5_parts$parsimony_rejected
pa_par_cq_d <- pa_cq_d; pa_par_cq_d$parsimony_rejected <- p5_parts$parsimony_rejected
pa_q23_par <- rbind(
  cbind(comparison = "Retributivists vs all other participants",
        welch_contrast(pa_par_d, "parsimony_rejected", "grp_rank",
                       alternative = "two.sided", label = pa_par_lab)),
  cbind(comparison = "Retributivists vs deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)",
        welch_contrast(pa_par_cq_d, "parsimony_rejected", "grp_vs_deter_incap",
                       alternative = "two.sided", label = pa_par_lab)))
# GUARDS.
#   4. Same columns as the rows above, so the export gains rows and nothing else;
#      the comparisons and group sizes are the 371 against the 577 and the 453.
#   5. The values the Supplement's Leniency paragraph quotes against the
#      deterrence- or incapacitation-first: M 4.62 against 4.04, d = 0.44
#      (section 5 below checks the rest).
stopifnot(identical(names(pa_q23_par), names(pa_q23)),
          identical(unique(pa_q23_par$comparison), unique(pa_q23$comparison)),
          identical(as.integer(pa_q23_par$n1), c(371L, 371L)),
          identical(as.integer(pa_q23_par$n2), c(577L, 453L)),
          !anyNA(pa_q23_par$d), !anyNA(pa_q23_par$d_lower))
# pa_shows(x, digits, "text") is TRUE when x, printed to `digits` decimals,
# reads exactly as the text the Supplement prints ("0.44", "-0.36"). It compares
# the printed digits rather than testing floating-point equality, so a value
# such as 0.445 cannot pass or fail by a rounding accident. Section 5 below
# uses it for every number the Supplement quotes from this chunk.
pa_shows <- function(x, digits, want) {
  identical(sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x), want)
}
stopifnot(pa_shows(pa_q23_par$M1[2], 2, "4.62"), pa_shows(pa_q23_par$M2[2], 2, "4.04"),
          pa_shows(pa_q23_par$d[2], 2, "0.44"))
pa_q23_n_before <- nrow(pa_q23)
pa_q23 <- rbind(pa_q23, pa_q23_par)
stopifnot(nrow(pa_q23) == pa_q23_n_before + 2L, pa_q23_n_before == 14L)
TABLES[["PAPER_dan_contrasts"]] <- pa_q23
show_table(pa_q23[, c("comparison", "outcome", "n1", "n2", "M1", "SD1", "M2", "SD2",
                      "t", "df", "p_two", "d", "d_lower", "d_upper")],
           "9.19E: retributivists against the others (two-sided, not registered)")

# --- 4. Agreement with the proportionality principle, as shares --------------------
# WHAT THIS COMPUTES: the share of each group who AGREED with the
#   proportionality principle ("Punishment should be proportionate to the
#   severity of the crime, no more and no less", 1 to 7), agreement being a
#   rating above 4, the scale midpoint (the rule H4, H12 and Figure S4 use),
#   and the difference between the retributivists' share and each comparison
#   group's share. The mean difference on the same item is the first row of
#   each comparison in PAPER_dan_contrasts; the share says how many agree,
#   which is what the paper's sentence about agreement is about.
# GROUPS: the retributivists (371, ranked retribution first); the deterrence- or
#   incapacitation-first (453, the main text's comparison group); all other
#   participants (577, the registered comparison group); the whole sample (948).
# METHODS.
#   - Each share has the exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval from prop_ci(),
#     the interval every other share in the paper carries (H4_shares, the H12
#     exports, Figure S4).
#   - Each difference is the retributivists' share minus the comparison group's,
#     in percentage points, with the Newcombe (1998) hybrid score 95% interval
#     (his method 10), the interval 06_princeton_talk_figures.Rmd's
#     share_diff() uses: each share's Wilson score interval, combined as in
#     pa_share_diff() below. It keeps close to 95% coverage at these sample
#     sizes and cannot run past plus or minus 100 points, which the simple Wald
#     interval (prop.test()'s own interval for a difference) can.
#   - Each difference's two-sided p is from the two-sample test of equal
#     proportions WITHOUT the continuity correction, prop.test(correct = FALSE):
#     the Pearson chi-square on the 2 x 2 table, identical to the pooled
#     two-proportion z test (a guard checks this, and z is exported beside it).
#     The p and the interval come from related but different methods (the p
#     from the pooled z, the interval from Wilson scores), as is usual for a
#     difference in shares; the export names both in ci_method and p_method.
# READS: pa_d$proportionality_principle and pa_d$grp_rank; pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap;
#   prop_ci() (0.3); h4_full$shares (8.1) and h11_h4$shares (9.1) for the guards.
# WRITES: TABLES[["PAPER_dan_prop_shares"]] (new): four share rows, then two
#   difference rows (all other participants first, as in PAPER_dan_contrasts).
#   Units: percent for the shares, percentage points for the differences.
# PAPER CLAIMS: Results, Part 2, "Most participants, 83.1%, agreed with the
#   proportionality principle"; General Discussion, "five in six retributivists
#   agreed with it. But note that similar levels of agreement were reported also
#   by the other participants"; Supplement S5 (Proportionality) and Table S19.
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED, two-sided. H4 concerns the whole sample (8.1 reports
#   its shares, and H11 repeats them among the retributivists in 9.1); no
#   comparison of agreement between groups was registered.
# DANGER: agreement is proportionality_principle > 4, STRICTLY above the
#   midpoint: the complement of H4's "Do NOT endorse strict proportionality
#   (proportionality <= 4)". A >= 4 cut would count the neutral answers as
#   agreement and change every share. The guards tie these counts to H4's.
# DANGER: the item is proportionality_principle, the direct item as answered,
#   never proportionality_jd (the registered three-item component, which
#   averages it with the two reversed departure items).
pa_ps_agree <- pa_d$proportionality_principle > 4
stopifnot(!anyNA(pa_ps_agree),
          identical(pa_d$proportionality_principle, pa_d$proportionality),
          identical(pa_cq_d$ResponseId, pa_d$ResponseId))
pa_ps_groups <- list(
  "Retributivists (ranked retribution first)" = pa_d$grp_rank %in% "Retributivist",
  "Deterrence- or incapacitation-first"       =
    pa_cq_d$grp_vs_deter_incap %in% "Deterrence or incapacitation first",
  "All other participants"                    = pa_d$grp_rank %in% "Other",
  "Whole sample"                              = rep(TRUE, nrow(pa_d)))
# GUARD: the groups are the 371, 453, 577 and 948; the retributivists and all
# the others partition the sample; the deterrence- or incapacitation-first are
# a subset of all the others.
stopifnot(identical(vapply(pa_ps_groups, sum, integer(1)),
                    c("Retributivists (ranked retribution first)" = 371L,
                      "Deterrence- or incapacitation-first" = 453L,
                      "All other participants" = 577L, "Whole sample" = 948L)),
          !any(pa_ps_groups[[1]] & pa_ps_groups[[3]]),
          all(pa_ps_groups[[1]] | pa_ps_groups[[3]]),
          all(pa_ps_groups[[3]][pa_ps_groups[[2]]]))
pa_ps_share <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_ps_groups), function(g) {
  s <- prop_ci(as.integer(pa_ps_agree[pa_ps_groups[[g]]]), g)
  data.frame(row_type = "Share agreeing (rating above 4), percent", group = g,
             n1 = s$n, k1 = s$k, n2 = NA_integer_, k2 = NA_integer_,
             estimate = 100 * s$prop, ci_lower = 100 * s$ci_lower,
             ci_upper = 100 * s$ci_upper,
             ci_method = "Exact (Clopper-Pearson), binom.test(), via prop_ci()",
             z = NA_real_, p_two = NA_real_, p_method = NA_character_,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

# THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO INDEPENDENT SHARES, k1/n1 - k2/n2 (as proportions,
# converted to percentage points below). Returns the difference, its Newcombe
# hybrid score 95% interval, the pooled z and the two-sided p. Each share's
# Wilson interval is taken from prop.test(correct = FALSE) on that share alone,
# and a guard checks it against the Wilson formula, so the interval cannot
# silently change meaning if prop.test() ever changes.
pa_share_diff <- function(k1, n1, k2, n2) {
  wilson <- function(k, n, z = stats::qnorm(0.975)) {
    p <- k / n
    (p + z^2 / (2 * n) + c(-1, 1) * z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))) /
      (1 + z^2 / n)
  }
  w1 <- as.numeric(stats::prop.test(k1, n1, correct = FALSE)$conf.int)
  w2 <- as.numeric(stats::prop.test(k2, n2, correct = FALSE)$conf.int)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(c(w1, w2), c(wilson(k1, n1), wilson(k2, n2)))))
  p1 <- k1 / n1; p2 <- k2 / n2; dlt <- p1 - p2
  # Newcombe's hybrid: the lower end borrows group 1's lower and group 2's
  # upper Wilson distances; the upper end the reverse.
  lo <- dlt - sqrt((p1 - w1[1])^2 + (w2[2] - p2)^2)
  hi <- dlt + sqrt((w1[2] - p1)^2 + (p2 - w2[1])^2)
  pt <- stats::prop.test(c(k1, k2), c(n1, n2), correct = FALSE)
  # GUARD: prop.test()'s p is the pooled two-proportion z test's p.
  pbar <- (k1 + k2) / (n1 + n2)
  z <- dlt / sqrt(pbar * (1 - pbar) * (1 / n1 + 1 / n2))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pt$p.value, 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(z)))))
  c(diff = dlt, lower = lo, upper = hi, z = z, p_two = pt$p.value)
}
pa_ps_cmp <- c(
  "Retributivists minus all other participants" = "All other participants",
  "Retributivists minus deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)" =
    "Deterrence- or incapacitation-first")
pa_ps_ret <- pa_ps_share[pa_ps_share$group == "Retributivists (ranked retribution first)", ]
pa_ps_diff <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_ps_cmp), function(cmp) {
  oth <- pa_ps_share[pa_ps_share$group == pa_ps_cmp[[cmp]], ]
  r <- pa_share_diff(pa_ps_ret$k1, pa_ps_ret$n1, oth$k1, oth$n1)
  data.frame(row_type = "Difference (retributivists minus comparison group), percentage points",
             group = cmp, n1 = pa_ps_ret$n1, k1 = pa_ps_ret$k1, n2 = oth$n1, k2 = oth$k1,
             estimate = 100 * r[["diff"]], ci_lower = 100 * r[["lower"]],
             ci_upper = 100 * r[["upper"]],
             ci_method = "Newcombe (1998) hybrid score (method 10), from Wilson score intervals",
             z = r[["z"]], p_two = r[["p_two"]],
             p_method = "Two-sample test of equal proportions, no continuity correction: prop.test(correct = FALSE)",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
pa_prop_shares <- rbind(pa_ps_share, pa_ps_diff)
pa_prop_shares$measure <- "Agreement with the proportionality principle (rating above 4)"
pa_prop_shares$alternative <- ifelse(is.na(pa_prop_shares$p_two), NA_character_, "two.sided")
pa_prop_shares <- pa_prop_shares[, c("measure", setdiff(names(pa_prop_shares), "measure"))]
# GUARDS.
#   1. The whole-sample count reproduces H4 (8.1): those agreeing are exactly
#      those H4 does not count as at or below the midpoint (948 - 160 = 788).
#   2. The retributivists' count reproduces H11's repeat of H4 (9.1):
#      371 - 58 = 313.
#   3. The whole sample's share is the paper's 83.1% (Results, Part 2), and its
#      exact interval is Figure S4's.
pa_h4_not <- h4_full$shares[h4_full$shares$measure ==
                              "Do NOT endorse strict proportionality (proportionality <= 4)", ]
pa_h11_not <- h11_h4$shares[h11_h4$shares$measure ==
                              "Do NOT endorse strict proportionality (proportionality <= 4)", ]
stopifnot(nrow(pa_h4_not) == 1, nrow(pa_h11_not) == 1,
          pa_ps_share$k1[pa_ps_share$group == "Whole sample"] == pa_h4_not$n - pa_h4_not$k,
          pa_ps_share$n1[pa_ps_share$group == "Whole sample"] == pa_h4_not$n,
          pa_ps_ret$k1 == pa_h11_not$n - pa_h11_not$k, pa_ps_ret$n1 == pa_h11_not$n,
          pa_shows(pa_ps_share$estimate[pa_ps_share$group == "Whole sample"], 1, "83.1"))
TABLES[["PAPER_dan_prop_shares"]] <- pa_prop_shares
show_table(pa_prop_shares[, c("row_type", "group", "n1", "k1", "n2", "k2", "estimate",
                              "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "z", "p_two")],
           "9.19E: agreement with the proportionality principle, shares and differences (two-sided, not registered)")

# --- 5. Every number Supplement S5 and Table S19 quote from this chunk ---------------
# WHAT THIS DOES: checks, value by value, that the numbers the Supplement prints
#   in S5 (Proportionality, Leniency) and in the rows of Table S19 headed "Not
#   registered (two-sided)" are what this knit produces, at the precision
#   printed. If a later change to the data or the scoring moves any of them, the
#   knit stops here and the Supplement has to be revisited. Nothing is computed.
# FORMAT: pa_shows() compares printed digits; minus signs are ASCII here, where
#   the Supplement prints a true minus sign. p values the Supplement prints as
#   "p < .001" are checked as below .001.
# DANGER: if a guard here fails, fix the Supplement's number (after checking
#   why it moved), never the guard alone.
pa_q_row <- function(cmp_all, var) {
  cmp <- if (cmp_all) "Retributivists vs all other participants" else
    "Retributivists vs deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)"
  r <- pa_q23[pa_q23$comparison == cmp & pa_q23$variable == var, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
# The means, SDs, t (against all others only, as Table S19 prints it), d and
# its interval for the five mean contrasts, in Table S19's order.
pa_quote <- list(
  proportionality_principle = list(M1 = "5.79", SD1 = "1.37", M2_all = "5.67", SD2_all = "1.36",
                                   M2_di = "5.71", t_all = "1.33",
                                   d_all = c("0.09", "-0.04", "0.22"), d_di = c("0.06", "-0.08", "0.20")),
  severity_1     = list(M1 = "3.71", SD1 = "1.84", M2_all = "3.11", SD2_all = "1.75",
                        M2_di = "3.19", t_all = "5.00",
                        d_all = c("0.33", "0.20", "0.47"), d_di = c("0.29", "0.15", "0.43")),
  severity_2     = list(M1 = "2.27", SD1 = "1.38", M2_all = "2.98", SD2_all = "1.63",
                        M2_di = "2.80", t_all = "-7.25",
                        d_all = c("-0.47", "-0.60", "-0.34"), d_di = c("-0.36", "-0.50", "-0.22")),
  severity_index = list(M1 = "4.72", SD1 = "1.13", M2_all = "4.06", SD2_all = "1.24",
                        M2_di = "4.20", t_all = "8.44",
                        d_all = c("0.56", "0.42", "0.69"), d_di = c("0.45", "0.31", "0.59")),
  parsimony_rejected = list(M1 = "4.62", SD1 = "1.23", M2_all = "3.90", SD2_all = "1.39",
                            M2_di = "4.04", t_all = "8.33",
                            d_all = c("0.55", "0.42", "0.68"), d_di = c("0.44", "0.30", "0.58")))
for (v in names(pa_quote)) {
  q <- pa_quote[[v]]; a <- pa_q_row(TRUE, v); b <- pa_q_row(FALSE, v)
  ok <- c(pa_shows(a$M1, 2, q$M1), pa_shows(a$SD1, 2, q$SD1),
          pa_shows(b$M1, 2, q$M1),
          pa_shows(a$M2, 2, q$M2_all), pa_shows(a$SD2, 2, q$SD2_all),
          pa_shows(b$M2, 2, q$M2_di), pa_shows(a$t, 2, q$t_all),
          pa_shows(c(a$d, a$d_lower, a$d_upper), 2, q$d_all),
          pa_shows(c(b$d, b$d_lower, b$d_upper), 2, q$d_di))
  if (!all(ok)) stop("Supplement S5 / Table S19 number moved for ", v, ": check ",
                     paste(which(!ok), collapse = ", "))
}
# p values: the principle's are printed (.18 against all others, .40 against
# the deterrence- or incapacitation-first); every other one is printed as
# p < .001. These rows' Welch df, printed as a range in Table S19's note, run
# from 763 to 880.
pa_pq <- pa_q23[pa_q23$variable %in% names(pa_quote), ]
stopifnot(pa_shows(pa_q_row(TRUE, "proportionality_principle")$p_two, 2, "0.18"),
          pa_shows(pa_q_row(FALSE, "proportionality_principle")$p_two, 2, "0.40"),
          all(pa_pq$p_two[pa_pq$variable != "proportionality_principle"] < .001),
          pa_shows(range(pa_pq$df), 0, c("763", "880")))
# The shares (percent, one decimal) and their differences (percentage points,
# one decimal, with the Newcombe interval and the two-sided p to two decimals).
pa_sh <- function(g) pa_prop_shares[pa_prop_shares$group == g, ]
stopifnot(
  pa_shows(pa_sh("Retributivists (ranked retribution first)")$estimate, 1, "84.4"),
  pa_shows(pa_sh("Deterrence- or incapacitation-first")$estimate, 1, "82.3"),
  pa_shows(pa_sh("All other participants")$estimate, 1, "82.3"),
  pa_shows(pa_sh("Whole sample")$estimate, 1, "83.1"),
  pa_shows(unlist(pa_sh("Retributivists minus deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)")[
    , c("estimate", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]), 1, c("2.0", "-3.2", "7.1")),
  pa_shows(pa_sh("Retributivists minus deterrence- or incapacitation-first (rehabilitation-first left out)")$p_two,
           2, "0.44"),
  pa_shows(unlist(pa_sh("Retributivists minus all other participants")[
    , c("estimate", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]), 1, c("2.0", "-2.9", "6.8")),
  pa_shows(pa_sh("Retributivists minus all other participants")$p_two, 2, "0.41"))
```

```{r phase9_paper_old_index}
# === 9.19F THE PAPER'S ANALYSES ON THE REGISTERED PUNITIVENESS SCORES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: reruns every analysis in which the paper's main text
# uses one of its two punitiveness scores with the registered score in its
# place: the full index (the eight-item scale and the first sentence, each
# standardized, then averaged, so the sentence carries half the weight) where
# the paper uses the six-part score, and the eight-item scale where it uses the
# standardized five-part score (the sentence side). Desert theory, revenge and
# everything else stay as in 9.19B to 9.19D, so any difference from those
# exports is the punitiveness score alone. This is the robustness rerun the
# Supplementary Materials report beside the paper's scoring. Produces
# PAPER_OLDINDEX_agreement (the four scores against one another),
# PAPER_OLDINDEX_H1, PAPER_OLDINDEX_steiger (H2, E2, H6's punitiveness row,
# H10), PAPER_OLDINDEX_H10_cors, PAPER_OLDINDEX_H8, PAPER_OLDINDEX_H11 (the
# retributive side of every grouping), PAPER_OLDINDEX_H12, PAPER_OLDINDEX_H21
# and PAPER_OLDINDEX_sentence_side.
# PREREG: the two scores are registered (prereg 5.2); their use in these
#         analyses, desert theory beside them and the deterrence- and
#         incapacitation-first comparison are not. Each test keeps the
#         direction and sidedness of the run it repeats in 9.19B to 9.19D.
# CONSUMES: pa_d, pa_old_full, pa_old_sr, pa_six, pa_five, PA_PUNIT,
#           PA_PUNIT_SR and the PA_ labels (9.19A); p5_d (7.4); pa_same_h1()
#           (9.19B); pa_h10_run(), pa_h10_cors_run() (9.19C);
#           pa_h11_summary(), pa_h12_run(), pa_h11_subs, pa_ratio_g,
#           pa_h12_sides, pa_h12_ratio, pa_h11_groupings, pa_cq_d (9.19D);
#           run_h1(), run_h2(), run_h8(), steiger_overlap(), cor_row(),
#           cont_reg(), welch_contrast(); the registered results h1_full,
#           h1_full_index (7.1), h2_full (7.2), h8_full (8.5), h11_h1 (9.1), h12
#           (9.2), e2 (9.15), contrasts_rank, contrasts_ratio, cq_contrasts,
#           cont_ratio, cont_resid (9.3, 9.10, 9.12b) for the guards.
#
# FILE NAMES. The exports are PAPER_OLDINDEX_*: the paper's analyses on the
# registered punitiveness scores. The six-part results are PAPER_H1 and the
# rest, so the names PAPER_SIX_* are retired (RETIRED_TABLES below): 10.1
# removes any file under those names that an earlier knit left in
# output/tables/, so that no one reads one as a current result.

# --- The copy with the registered scores restored -----------------------------------
# pa_d with its two punitiveness columns set back to the registered scores. The
# column names are the same as in pa_d, so every function of 9.19B to 9.19D
# runs on it unchanged; only the labels differ.
pa_old_d <- pa_d
pa_old_d$punitiveness_full <- pa_old_full
pa_old_d$punitiveness      <- pa_old_sr
PA_OLD_LAB    <- "Punitiveness (full index)"
PA_OLD_LAB_SR <- "Punitiveness (eight-item scale)"
# GUARD: the copy differs from d only in desert and just deserts (which carry
# desert theory, as in pa_d); its punitiveness columns are the registered ones.
pa_old_changed <- names(d)[!vapply(names(d), function(v)
  isTRUE(all.equal(d[[v]], pa_old_d[[v]])), logical(1))]
stopifnot(setequal(pa_old_changed, c("deserved", "just_deserts")),
          identical(pa_old_d$punitiveness_full, d$punitiveness_full),
          identical(pa_old_d$punitiveness, d$punitiveness))
RETIRED_TABLES <- paste0("PAPER_SIX_", c("agreement", "H1", "steiger", "H8", "H11",
                                         "H12", "H21"))
stopifnot(!any(RETIRED_TABLES %in% names(TABLES)))

# --- How closely the four scores agree -------------------------------------------------
# Every pair of the paper's two scores and the two registered ones, and 7.4's
# plain five-part mean against the standardized one. Two-sided intervals. The
# first two rows are the six-part score against the two registered scores.
pa_ag_d <- data.frame(six = pa_six, full = pa_old_full, eight = pa_old_sr,
                      five = pa_five, five_raw = p5_d$punit_parts5)
pa_ag_lab <- c(six = PA_LAB, full = PA_OLD_LAB, eight = PA_OLD_LAB_SR, five = PA_LAB_SR,
               five_raw = "Punitiveness (five attitude components, plain mean of the raw parts; 7.4)")
pa_ag_pairs <- list(c("full", "six"), c("eight", "six"), c("five", "six"),
                    c("full", "eight"), c("full", "five"), c("eight", "five"),
                    c("five_raw", "five"))
pa_old_agree <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pa_ag_pairs, function(pr)
  cor_row(pa_ag_d, pr[1], pr[2], alternative = "two.sided",
          label_x = pa_ag_lab[[pr[1]]], label_y = pa_ag_lab[[pr[2]]])))
# GUARD: the six-part score against the full index (.945) and the eight-item
# scale (.972), and the standardized five-part score against the eight-item
# scale (about .99), as 9.19A checked them.
stopifnot(round(pa_old_agree$r[1:2], 3) == c(0.945, 0.972),
          round(pa_old_agree$r[6], 2) == 0.99)
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_agreement"]] <- pa_old_agree
show_table(pa_old_agree[, c("x", "y", "n", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")],
           "9.19F: the paper's two punitiveness scores and the two registered ones")

# --- H1, H2, E2, H6's punitiveness row, H8, H10 --------------------------------------
pa_old_h1 <- run_h1(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT)
pa_old_h10 <- rbind(pa_h10_run(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT, PA_OLD_LAB),
                    pa_h10_run(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, PA_OLD_LAB_SR))
pa_old_st <- rbind(
  cbind(test = "H2: hostile aggression vs crime concerns (one-sided)",
        punitiveness = PA_OLD_LAB, run_h2(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT)),
  cbind(test = "H2: hostile aggression vs crime concerns (one-sided)",
        punitiveness = PA_OLD_LAB_SR, run_h2(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT_SR)),
  cbind(test = "E2: hostile vs Durkheimian solidarity (one-sided)",
        punitiveness = PA_OLD_LAB,
        steiger_overlap(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT, "solidarity_hostile", "solidarity_durk",
                        alternative = "greater",
                        label = "r(punitiveness, hostile solidarity) > r(punitiveness, Durkheimian solidarity)")),
  cbind(test = "H6 companion: severity index vs principle (two-sided)",
        punitiveness = PA_OLD_LAB,
        steiger_overlap(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT, "severity_index", "proportionality_principle",
                        alternative = "two.sided",
                        label = "r(punitiveness, severity index) vs r(punitiveness, principle)")),
  cbind(test = paste0("H10: revenge vs desert theory (", pa_old_h10$sidedness, ")"),
        pa_old_h10[, setdiff(names(pa_old_h10), "sidedness")]))
pa_old_h8 <- run_h8(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT)
pa_old_h8$y <- PA_OLD_LAB
# GUARDS: with the registered scores restored, the functions of 9.19B to 9.19D
# reproduce the registered runs: H1 on the full index (7.1's robustness run)
# and on the eight-item scale (7.1), H2 and E2 on the eight-item scale (7.2,
# 9.15), H8 on the eight-item scale (8.5); and the same H1 call with the
# paper's score in place reproduces 9.19B, so the two exports differ in the
# score alone.
stopifnot(pa_same_h1(pa_old_h1, h1_full_index),
          pa_same_h1(run_h1(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT_SR), h1_full),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_st$diff[2], h2_full$diff)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_st$z[2], h2_full$z)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(steiger_overlap(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, "solidarity_hostile",
                                           "solidarity_durk", alternative = "greater",
                                           label = "")$diff, e2$diff)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(run_h8(pa_old_d, punit = PA_PUNIT_SR)$r, h8_full$r)),
          pa_same_h1(run_h1(pa_d, punit = PA_PUNIT), pa_h1))
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H1"]]      <- pa_old_h1
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_steiger"]] <- pa_old_st
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H8"]]      <- pa_old_h8
show_table(pa_old_h1[, c("y", "n", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_one_sided", "p_BH_one_sided")],
           "9.19F: H1 on the full index (one-sided, BH across the twelve)")
show_table(pa_old_st[, c("test", "punitiveness", "r_jk", "r_jh", "diff", "diff_lower",
                         "diff_upper", "z", "p")],
           "9.19F: H2, E2, H6's punitiveness row and H10 on the registered scores")

# --- H11 and H12 on the retributive side of every grouping --------------------------
# The same summary as 9.19D with the full index, except under the ratio
# grouping, where the eight-item scale is used (the ratio is built from the
# sentence). The subsets are 9.19D's people, taken from pa_old_d.
pa_old_subs <- lapply(pa_h11_subs, function(s)
  pa_old_d[match(s$ResponseId, pa_old_d$ResponseId), ])
pa_old_h11 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_old_subs), function(g)
  suppressWarnings(pa_h11_summary(pa_old_subs[[g]], g,
                                  punit = if (g == pa_ratio_g) PA_PUNIT_SR else PA_PUNIT,
                                  lab = if (g == pa_ratio_g) PA_OLD_LAB_SR else PA_OLD_LAB))))
pa_old_h12 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pa_h12_sides), function(g)
  pa_h12_run(pa_old_d[pa_h12_sides[[g]] %in% TRUE, ], g,
             if (g == pa_h12_ratio) PA_PUNIT_SR else PA_PUNIT,
             lab = if (g == pa_h12_ratio) PA_OLD_LAB_SR else PA_OLD_LAB)))
# GUARDS.
#   1. The subsets are 9.19D's people.
#   2. Among retributivists, H1 on the eight-item scale reproduces 9.1's run,
#      and H12 on the eight-item scale reproduces 9.2's correlations.
#   3. The rows that read no punitiveness column (H3 to H7, H9, and H6's
#      desert-theory rows) are 9.19D's, grouping by grouping.
stopifnot(identical(unname(lapply(pa_old_subs, `[[`, "ResponseId")),
                    unname(lapply(pa_h11_subs, `[[`, "ResponseId"))))
pa_old_retrib <- pa_old_subs[["Ranking (retribution first)"]]
pa_old_h12_chk <- pa_h12_run(pa_old_retrib, "check", PA_PUNIT_SR, lab = "check")
stopifnot(pa_same_h1(run_h1(pa_old_retrib, punit = PA_PUNIT_SR), h11_h1),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_h12_chk$r[seq_len(nrow(h12_spec))],
                           h12$r_with_punitiveness[match(h12_spec$label, h12$attitude)])))
pa_no_p <- !grepl("^(H1_|H2_|H8_|H10_)", pa_old_h11$quantity)
stopifnot(identical(pa_old_h11$quantity, pa_h11_groupings$quantity),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_h11$value[pa_no_p], pa_h11_groupings$value[pa_no_p])))
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H11"]] <- pa_old_h11
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H12"]] <- pa_old_h12

# Each side of H10 with its own 95% interval (two-sided), on the two registered
# scores, in the whole sample and among retributivists, as 9.19C and 9.19D
# report them on the paper's scores.
pa_old_h10_cors <- rbind(
  pa_h10_cors_run(pa_old_d, "Whole sample", labs = c(PA_OLD_LAB, PA_OLD_LAB_SR)),
  pa_h10_cors_run(pa_old_retrib, "Retributivists", labs = c(PA_OLD_LAB, PA_OLD_LAB_SR)))
# GUARD: the whole-sample full-index rows carry the correlations the Steiger
# rows above compare (desert theory, then revenge).
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_h10_cors$r[1:2], c(pa_old_h10$r_jh[1], pa_old_h10$r_jk[1]))))
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H10_cors"]] <- pa_old_h10_cors

# --- H21: retributivists against the others on punitiveness --------------------------
# One-sided, retributivists higher, as registered; against all other
# participants and against the deterrence- and incapacitation-first; on the
# full index.
pa_old_cq <- pa_cq_d
pa_old_cq$punitiveness_full <- pa_old_full
pa_old_cq$punitiveness      <- pa_old_sr
pa_old_h21 <- rbind(
  cbind(comparison = "Retributivists vs all other participants",
        welch_contrast(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT, "grp_rank", alternative = "greater",
                       label = PA_OLD_LAB)),
  cbind(comparison = "Retributivists vs deterrence- or incapacitation-first",
        welch_contrast(pa_old_cq, PA_PUNIT, "grp_vs_deter_incap", alternative = "greater",
                       label = PA_OLD_LAB)))
# GUARD: both rows are the registered full-index rows of the ranking run (9.3)
# and of 9.12b's run.
pa_old_full_lab <- contrast_spec$label[contrast_spec$outcome == "punitiveness_full"]
stopifnot(identical(pa_old_cq$ResponseId, pa_old_d$ResponseId),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_h21$d, c(contrasts_rank$d[contrasts_rank$outcome == pa_old_full_lab],
                                           cq_contrasts$d[cq_contrasts$outcome == pa_old_full_lab]))))
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_H21"]] <- pa_old_h21
show_table(pa_old_h21[, c("comparison", "n1", "n2", "M1", "M2", "t", "df", "p_dir", "d",
                          "d_lower", "d_upper")],
           "9.19F: H21 on the full index (one-sided)")

# --- The sentence side on the eight-item scale ---------------------------------------
# The analyses in which the paper uses the standardized five-part score, with
# the eight-item scale in its place: the sentencing ratio's correlation with
# punitiveness (two-sided), the ratio and the residualized second sentence as
# continuous predictors of punitiveness (one-sided, as registered), and H21
# under the ratio grouping (one-sided). Each is a registered computation, so
# each reproduces a registered export (guard below); they are gathered here so
# that the Supplement reads the robustness rerun from one family of files.
pa_old_row <- function(analysis, n, est, lo, hi, p_two, p_dir) data.frame(
  analysis = analysis, punitiveness = PA_OLD_LAB_SR, n = as.numeric(n), estimate = est,
  ci_lower = lo, ci_upper = hi, p_two = p_two, p_dir = p_dir, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
pa_old_rc   <- cor_row(pa_old_d, "sentence_ratio", PA_PUNIT_SR, alternative = "two.sided")
pa_old_cr   <- cont_reg(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, "sentence_ratio", alternative = "greater")
pa_old_cs   <- cont_reg(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, "sentence_resid", alternative = "greater")
pa_old_h21r <- welch_contrast(pa_old_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, "grp_ratio", alternative = "greater",
                              label = PA_OLD_LAB_SR)
pa_old_ss <- rbind(
  pa_old_row("Sentencing ratio with punitiveness (r, two-sided)", pa_old_rc$n, pa_old_rc$r,
             pa_old_rc$ci_lower, pa_old_rc$ci_upper, pa_old_rc$p_two, pa_old_rc$p_dir),
  pa_old_row("Sentencing ratio, continuous (beta, one-sided)", pa_old_cr$n, pa_old_cr$beta,
             pa_old_cr$ci_lower, pa_old_cr$ci_upper, pa_old_cr$p_two, pa_old_cr$p_dir),
  pa_old_row("Second sentence residualized on the first, continuous (beta, one-sided)",
             pa_old_cs$n, pa_old_cs$beta, pa_old_cs$ci_lower, pa_old_cs$ci_upper,
             pa_old_cs$p_two, pa_old_cs$p_dir),
  pa_old_row("H21 under the sentencing-ratio grouping (d, one-sided)",
             pa_old_h21r$n1 + pa_old_h21r$n2, pa_old_h21r$d, pa_old_h21r$d_lower,
             pa_old_h21r$d_upper, pa_old_h21r$p_two, pa_old_h21r$p_dir))
# GUARD: each row reproduces the registered run it repeats: the ratio and the
# residualized-sentence rows of 9.10's continuous runs, and the H21 row of the
# ratio grouping; the estimate column holds r, beta, beta and d in that order.
pa_old_sr_lab <- contrast_spec$label[contrast_spec$outcome == "punitiveness"]
stopifnot(nrow(pa_old_ss) == 4,
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_old_ss$estimate[2:4],
                           c(cont_ratio$beta[cont_ratio$outcome == pa_old_sr_lab],
                             cont_resid$beta[cont_resid$outcome == pa_old_sr_lab],
                             contrasts_ratio$d[contrasts_ratio$outcome == pa_old_sr_lab]))))
TABLES[["PAPER_OLDINDEX_sentence_side"]] <- pa_old_ss
show_table(pa_old_ss, "9.19F: the sentence side on the eight-item scale")
```

```{r phase9_paper_just_deserts}
# === 9.19G H7, H9 AND H10 AGAINST THE PAPER'S JUST-DESERTS SCORE ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: builds the paper's just-deserts score, the plain mean of
# desert theory (Retribution_1 to _5) and the proportionality principle item,
# both on the 1 to 7 scale; reports how its two parts go together; and reruns
# H7, H9 and H10, in the whole sample and among the retributivists (H11),
# against it, with the registered test functions. 9.19C and 9.19D report the
# same tests against desert theory; the paper reports both. Produces
# PAPER_JD_parts, PAPER_JD_H7, PAPER_JD_H9, PAPER_JD_H10, PAPER_JD_H10_cors,
# PAPER_JD_H11_H7, PAPER_JD_H11_H9, PAPER_JD_H11_H10 and PAPER_person_scores
# (the paper's scores, participant by participant).
# PREREG: NOT REGISTERED as a scoring. The registered just deserts (prereg 5.4)
#         averages desert (Retribution_1 to _4) with the three-item
#         proportionality component; it stays in `d` and the registered H7, H9
#         and H10 (8.4, 8.6, 8.7) use it. The tests here are the registered
#         tests (6.4) with this score in place of that one, keeping their
#         direction and sidedness: H7's just-deserts half two-sided, H9 paired
#         and one-sided (just deserts higher), H10 one-sided (revenge more
#         closely tied to punitiveness), with H10 also given two-sided, as in
#         9.19C. The co-authors set this score on 27 Sep 2026.
# CONSUMES: pa_d, pa_retrib, pa_retribution_items, pa_scores, PA_PUNIT,
#           PA_PUNIT_SR and the PA_ labels (9.19A, 9.19D); pa_relabel_h7(),
#           pa_h7, pa_h9 (9.19C); pa_h11_h7, pa_h11_h9 (9.19D); run_h7(),
#           run_h9(), run_h10(), steiger_overlap(), cor_row(), p5_alpha()
#           (7.0, 7.4).
#
# WHY A RAW MEAN. H9 compares the mean agreement with just deserts with the
# mean agreement with revenge, on the items' own 1 to 7 scale. A standardized
# score has a mean of 0 and could not be set against revenge's mean; the two
# parts are on the same 1 to 7 scale, so a plain mean needs no standardizing.
# WHY A SECOND COPY. run_h7(), run_h9() and run_h10() read the column
# `just_deserts`. pa_jd_d is pa_d with that column carrying the paper's
# just-deserts score, so the registered functions run on it unchanged. Its
# `deserved` column still carries desert theory, as in pa_d.

# --- The score ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GUARD: the principle item is present for everyone and on the 1 to 7 scale,
# so the mean is defined for every participant and stays on that scale.
stopifnot("proportionality_principle" %in% names(d),
          !anyNA(d$proportionality_principle),
          all(d$proportionality_principle %in% 1:7))
pa_jd <- rowMeans(cbind(pa_retribution_items, d$proportionality_principle))
pa_jd_d <- pa_d
pa_jd_d$just_deserts <- pa_jd
# GUARD: the second copy differs from pa_d in just_deserts only.
pa_jd_changed <- names(pa_d)[!vapply(names(pa_d), function(v)
  isTRUE(all.equal(pa_d[[v]], pa_jd_d[[v]])), logical(1))]
stopifnot(identical(pa_jd_changed, "just_deserts"),
          identical(pa_jd_d$deserved, pa_retribution_items))
pa_jd_retrib <- pa_jd_d[!is.na(pa_jd_d$retributivist) & pa_jd_d$retributivist == 1, ]
stopifnot(identical(pa_jd_retrib$ResponseId, pa_retrib$ResponseId))

# --- Do the two parts go together? ---------------------------------------------------
# Their correlation (two-sided, since no direction was predicted for this
# pairing), and alpha two ways: of the two scores as they stand (the reliability
# of the raw mean the paper uses) and of the two standardized (as the
# registered H6 test computes it for its two parts). With two parts, alpha
# depends on nothing but their correlation and spreads.
pa_jd_parts_run <- function(data, who) {
  cr <- cor_row(data.frame(a = data$retribution_items, b = data$proportionality_principle),
                "a", "b", alternative = "two.sided",
                label_x = PA_DT, label_y = "Proportionality principle")
  cbind(sample = who, cr[, c("x", "y", "n", "r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "p_two")],
        alpha_raw = p5_alpha(data.frame(data$retribution_items, data$proportionality_principle)),
        alpha_standardized = p5_alpha(data.frame(scale(data$retribution_items),
                                                 scale(data$proportionality_principle))),
        M_just_deserts = mean(data$just_deserts), SD_just_deserts = stats::sd(data$just_deserts),
        M_desert_theory = mean(data$retribution_items),
        M_principle = mean(data$proportionality_principle),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
pa_jd_parts <- rbind(pa_jd_parts_run(pa_jd_d, "Whole sample"),
                     pa_jd_parts_run(pa_jd_retrib, "Retributivists"))
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_parts"]] <- pa_jd_parts
show_table(pa_jd_parts, "9.19G: the two parts of the paper's just-deserts score")

# --- H7, H9, H10 in the whole sample ---------------------------------------------------
# H7: run_h7() on pa_jd_d; its revenge half is 9.19C's, and its just-deserts
# half is labelled with the paper's score.
pa_jd_h7 <- pa_relabel_h7(run_h7(pa_jd_d), lab = PA_JD)
# H9: run_h9() returns two paired tests against revenge: just deserts (here the
# paper's score) and `deserved` (here desert theory, identical to 9.19C's H9).
pa_jd_h9 <- run_h9(pa_jd_d)
pa_jd_h9$comparison <- c(paste(PA_JD, "vs revenge"), paste(PA_DT, "vs revenge"))
# H10: revenge against the paper's just deserts, on each punitiveness score of
# the paper, one-sided in the registered direction (run_h10(), the registered
# function) and two-sided.
pa_jd_h10_run <- function(data, punit, who) rbind(
  cbind(punitiveness = who, sidedness = "one-sided, registered direction",
        run_h10(data, punit = punit)),
  cbind(punitiveness = who, sidedness = "two-sided",
        steiger_overlap(data, punit, "revenge", "just_deserts", alternative = "two.sided",
                        label = "r(punitiveness, revenge) vs r(punitiveness, just deserts)")))
pa_jd_h10 <- rbind(pa_jd_h10_run(pa_jd_d, PA_PUNIT, PA_LAB),
                   pa_jd_h10_run(pa_jd_d, PA_PUNIT_SR, PA_LAB_SR))
# Each side of H10 with its own 95% interval (two-sided), in the whole sample
# and among retributivists.
pa_jd_cors_run <- function(data, who) do.call(rbind, lapply(c(PA_PUNIT, PA_PUNIT_SR), function(pu) {
  lab <- ifelse(pu == PA_PUNIT, PA_LAB, PA_LAB_SR)
  cbind(sample = who, rbind(
    cor_row(data, pu, "just_deserts", alternative = "two.sided", label_x = lab, label_y = PA_JD),
    cor_row(data, pu, "revenge", alternative = "two.sided", label_x = lab, label_y = "Revenge")))
}))
pa_jd_cors <- rbind(pa_jd_cors_run(pa_jd_d, "Whole sample"),
                    pa_jd_cors_run(pa_jd_retrib, "Retributivists"))
# GUARDS.
#   1. The revenge half of H7 and the desert-theory row of H9 are 9.19C's.
#   2. The Steiger rows read the scores they name.
#   3. The values the co-authors were shown before settling the score: on the
#      six-part score, revenge .676 against just deserts .432, a difference of
#      .244 [.188, .301], Z = 8.70; H9, M = 5.66 against 4.14, d = 1.08.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h7$r[pa_jd_h7$y == "Revenge"], pa_h7$r[pa_h7$y == "Revenge"])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h9$d[2], pa_h9$d)), isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h9$t[2], pa_h9$t)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h10$r_jh[1], stats::cor(pa_six, pa_jd))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h10$r_jk[1], stats::cor(pa_six, d$revenge))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_cors$r[1], pa_jd_h10$r_jh[1])))
stopifnot(round(pa_jd_h10$r_jk[1], 3) == 0.676, round(pa_jd_h10$r_jh[1], 3) == 0.432,
          round(c(pa_jd_h10$diff[1], pa_jd_h10$diff_lower[1], pa_jd_h10$diff_upper[1]), 3) ==
            c(0.244, 0.188, 0.301),
          round(pa_jd_h10$z[1], 2) == 8.70,
          round(c(pa_jd_h9$M1[1], pa_jd_h9$M2[1], pa_jd_h9$d[1]), 2) == c(5.66, 4.14, 1.08))
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H7"]]       <- pa_jd_h7
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H9"]]       <- pa_jd_h9
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H10"]]      <- pa_jd_h10
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H10_cors"]] <- pa_jd_cors
show_table(pa_jd_h9[, c("comparison", "n", "M1", "M2", "t", "df", "p_dir", "d",
                        "d_lower", "d_upper")],
           "9.19G: H9, the paper's just deserts and desert theory against revenge (paired, one-sided)")
show_table(pa_jd_h10[, c("punitiveness", "sidedness", "r_jk", "r_jh", "r_kh", "diff",
                         "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z", "p")],
           "9.19G: H10, revenge against the paper's just deserts as correlates of punitiveness")

# --- The same three among the retributivists (H11) --------------------------------------
pa_jd_h11_h7  <- pa_relabel_h7(run_h7(pa_jd_retrib), lab = PA_JD)
pa_jd_h11_h9  <- run_h9(pa_jd_retrib)
pa_jd_h11_h9$comparison <- c(paste(PA_JD, "vs revenge, retributivists"),
                             paste(PA_DT, "vs revenge, retributivists"))
pa_jd_h11_h10 <- rbind(pa_jd_h10_run(pa_jd_retrib, PA_PUNIT, PA_LAB),
                       pa_jd_h10_run(pa_jd_retrib, PA_PUNIT_SR, PA_LAB_SR))
# GUARD: the revenge half of H7 and the desert-theory row of H9 are 9.19D's.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h11_h7$r[pa_jd_h11_h7$y == "Revenge"],
                           pa_h11_h7$r[pa_h11_h7$y == "Revenge"])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_jd_h11_h9$d[2], pa_h11_h9$d)))
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H11_H7"]]  <- pa_jd_h11_h7
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H11_H9"]]  <- pa_jd_h11_h9
TABLES[["PAPER_JD_H11_H10"]] <- pa_jd_h11_h10
show_table(pa_jd_h11_h10[, c("punitiveness", "sidedness", "r_jk", "r_jh", "diff",
                             "diff_lower", "diff_upper", "z", "p")],
           "9.19G: H10 against the paper's just deserts, among retributivists")

# --- The paper's scores, participant by participant ---------------------------------
pa_scores$just_deserts <- pa_jd
stopifnot(identical(pa_scores$ResponseId, pa_jd_d$ResponseId), !anyNA(pa_scores))
TABLES[["PAPER_person_scores"]] <- pa_scores
```

```{r phase9_paper_moderators}
# === 9.19H TABLE S23 WITH THE PAPER'S PUNITIVENESS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: refits 9.18C's eight moderation models with punitiveness
# scored as the paper scores it: the six-part score where relative retribution
# predicts punitiveness, and the standardized five-part score where the
# sentencing ratio does (the ratio is built from the sentence, and the six-part
# score contains it). The other four models (the hostile aggression cluster and
# the first sentence on relative retribution) read no rescored column and are
# refitted only so the table is complete; they reproduce 9.18C exactly. Produces
# PAPER_MOD_interactions and PAPER_MOD_simple_slopes.
# PREREG: 6.6, exploratory, as in 9.18C: no outcome, model or direction was
#         registered; every p is two-sided and uncorrected. The punitiveness
#         scores are not registered (9.19A).
# CONSUMES: pa_d, PA_LAB, PA_LAB_SR, pa_six, pa_five (9.19A); mod_fit(),
#           mod_specs, mod_labels, mod_results, mod_slopes (9.18B, 9.18C).
#
# HOW. mod_fit() reads `d` and `mod_labels` from the document. pa_mod_fit is
# the same function, byte for byte, evaluated where `d` is pa_d and
# `mod_labels` carries the paper's labels, so the model, its centring, its
# guards and its simple slopes are 9.18C's. Nothing in 9.18 is changed, and
# `d` is not touched.
# UNITS. Both paper scores average standardized parts, so a slope on
# punitiveness is in standard-deviation units of the parts, not in points of
# the 1 to 7 scale as in 9.18C.

# The grid: 9.18C's, with the punitiveness outcome named by the pa_d column
# that carries the intended score.
pa_mod_specs <- mod_specs
pa_mod_specs$y[pa_mod_specs$y == "punitiveness" & pa_mod_specs$x == "retribution_rel"] <-
  "punitiveness_full"   # in pa_d: the six-part score
# The ratio rows keep "punitiveness", which in pa_d is the five-part score.
# GUARDS: the grid is 9.18C's apart from that one change; no ratio row reads the
# six-part score (it contains the sentence the ratio is built from); and the
# two columns carry the scores their labels will name.
stopifnot(nrow(pa_mod_specs) == 8,
          identical(pa_mod_specs$x, mod_specs$x), identical(pa_mod_specs$m, mod_specs$m),
          sum(pa_mod_specs$y != mod_specs$y) == 2,
          !any(pa_mod_specs$x == "sentence_ratio" &
               pa_mod_specs$y %in% c("Sentence1", "Sentence1_z", "Sentence2",
                                     "sentence_resid", "punitiveness_full")),
          identical(pa_d$punitiveness_full, pa_six), identical(pa_d$punitiveness, pa_five))
pa_mod_labels <- c(mod_labels, punitiveness_full = PA_LAB)
pa_mod_labels[["punitiveness"]] <- PA_LAB_SR
pa_mod_fit <- mod_fit
environment(pa_mod_fit) <- list2env(list(d = pa_d, mod_labels = pa_mod_labels),
                                    parent = environment(mod_fit))
pa_mod_out <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pa_mod_specs)), function(i)
  pa_mod_fit(pa_mod_specs$y[i], pa_mod_specs$x[i], pa_mod_specs$m[i]))
pa_mod_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pa_mod_out, `[[`, "row"))
pa_mod_slopes  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pa_mod_out, `[[`, "slopes"))
if (!all(pa_mod_slopes$inside_range))
  cat("NOTE: some +/-1 SD probe values lie outside the observed range; see inside_range.\n")
# GUARDS.
#   1. The four models that read no punitiveness column reproduce 9.18C row
#      for row, slopes included, so the copy runs the registered models.
#   2. Each punitiveness model's interaction equals a plain uncentred fit of
#      the intended score on the predictor, the moderator and their product
#      (centring leaves the interaction unchanged), fitted on d's columns
#      directly, so the rows carry the score their labels name.
pa_same_rows <- !(mod_specs$y %in% "punitiveness")
stopifnot(nrow(pa_mod_results) == 8, nrow(pa_mod_slopes) == 24,
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_mod_results[pa_same_rows, ], mod_results[pa_same_rows, ],
                           check.attributes = FALSE)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(pa_mod_slopes[rep(pa_same_rows, each = 3), ],
```
